results.name: network_game_client_send_settings_ack
results.evidence: Switches on the connection-state field at offset 0xeda (only states 2/3 do anything); on match it looks up an outgoing item via FUN_004deaf0 and commits its size through the write/flush pair (FUN_004cf8f0/FUN_004ddb60) shared by every other packet-queue helper in this file; called only from the case-8 message decode handler (0x4dbe50) while the client is receiving game settings.
results.summary: Builds and queues a small acknowledgement message while the local connection is in state 2 or 3 (used right after receiving the game-settings/map message); a no-op otherwise.

results.name: network_game_send_game_options_message
results.evidence: Copies an 8-dword source record (in_EDX) into a scratch buffer, then calls the already-named data_packet_group_encode_packet(...,0x12,1) with a large (0x600-byte) output buffer, and on success commits the encoded size through the same FUN_004cf8f0/FUN_004ddb60 enqueue pattern used elsewhere for outgoing messages.
results.summary: Encodes a large (up to 0x600-byte) outgoing network-game message (type id 0x12) from an 8-dword source record and queues it for transmission.

results.name: network_game_client_commit_queued_message
results.evidence: Only runs when the connection state field (in_ECX+0xeda) equals 2; looks up a pending outgoing item via FUN_004deaf0 and commits it with the same FUN_004cf8f0(1)/FUN_004cf8f0(size)/FUN_004ddb60 tail seen at the end of FUN_004d9f50, but performs no encoding of its own.
results.summary: Commits a previously-staged outgoing message to the send queue while the connection is in state 2; otherwise a no-op.

results.name: network_game_action_dispatch
results.evidence: Reentrancy-guarded (DAT_0071c2c0) dispatch on a type field read from *in_EAX+4, with up to 0x37 cases; several cases call the already-named item_add_ammunition, player_update_client_local_player_update_from_network and player_update_client_local_player_vehicle_update_from_network, and the whole table is executed for DAT_00719720==1 while only a small subset of cases (goto targets) runs for DAT_00719720==2 -- i.e. host applies every action type, client only a privileged subset.
results.summary: Applies a single queued network-game action by type id, calling the specific per-type handler (ammo pickups, player/vehicle network updates, etc.); the full table runs when acting as host, only a restricted subset when acting as client.

results.name: network_game_search_result_is_active
results.evidence: Reads a per-entry timestamp at offset 0x18 and a validity byte at 0x12d off an unaff_ESI record and returns whether less than 0x1771 (6001) ms have elapsed since the timestamp; the same two offsets (0x18 timestamp, 0x12d valid flag) are used to expire entries in FUN_004da7d0's fixed 9-entry table.
results.summary: Tests whether a single entry in the 9-slot game-search/pending-connection record table is still within its ~6 second freshness window.

results.name: network_game_search_results_add_or_update
results.evidence: Walks a fixed table of 9 0x130-byte records, first expiring stale entries (>6000ms via QueryPerformanceCounter), then finds an entry matching the incoming record's key or an existing empty/free slot, and copies in a name (wcsncpy with "???" fallback), map/gametype/player-count style short fields, a 0x21-dword info block, and dedicated/flag bits derived from the incoming record -- consistent with a LAN game-search results cache with per-server name-collision handling.
results.summary: Adds a newly-received game-announcement record to (or refreshes an existing entry in) a fixed 9-slot list of discovered network games, expiring entries older than about 6 seconds.

results.name: network_game_client_join_update
results.evidence: Records a timestamp into the channel context, then when DAT_0071c2d4 (active game/session pointer) is zero drives the connect attempt via FUN_004dd110/FUN_004db180/FUN_004d9400, and when a specific sub-state (*(short*)(iVar1+4)==1) is active builds a connect-request payload (local/loopback address, port from DAT_00698208, player name via wcsncpy) and calls FUN_004e0790/FUN_004d8cf0 to transmit and progress the connection.
results.summary: Per-tick update that drives the client's join-a-server handshake: services the transport, and once a specific waiting sub-state is reached builds and sends the address/name connect request.

results.name: network_game_client_update_connecting_status
results.evidence: References the "Loading" string, checks channel validity/flags (piVar4[0x2a3], socket handle at *piVar4), branches on an error-code-like short at offset 0xe, retries a connect attempt every 3000ms via FUN_004db4c0 when otherwise healthy, and otherwise sets the DAT_00718fa4 error code and the DAT_00718f8c UI status state used elsewhere for "Connecting"/"Loading" text.
results.summary: Per-tick state machine that updates the join UI status text/timeout and retries the connect attempt while the client channel is not yet fully connected.

results.name: network_game_host_broadcast_presence
results.evidence: Every 1000ms (guarded via the same QueryPerformanceCounter/__alldiv pattern used throughout this file) calls FUN_00442640(1), builds a message from the global string at DAT_00719879 via strncpy, encodes it through FUN_004deaf0 and commits it via the shared FUN_004cf8f0/FUN_004ddb60 enqueue tail.
results.summary: Periodically (every second) builds and queues a short broadcast-style message carrying a global status string, consistent with a hosted-game LAN presence announcement.

results.name: network_game_host_update_lobby
results.evidence: Checks the channel's flag word (piVar2[0x2a3] bits 1/2/4) and that its primary child socket is valid and connected before calling FUN_004dadb0 (broadcast presence), FUN_004dd110 (channel service) and FUN_004db180 (process incoming messages) in sequence, else sets the DAT_00718fa4 error code used by the connecting-state machine.
results.summary: Per-tick update for a hosted game: broadcasts presence, services the network channel, and drains incoming messages while the host's socket is healthy.

results.name: network_game_client_update
results.evidence: Uses the strings "current ping time[%d] samples received[%d] samples sent[%d]\n" and "current time delta[%d] latency[%d] server time[%d]\n" to debug-print fields at offsets 0xad0/0xad2/0xad4 that match the ping/pong sample counters updated by the paired send/receive-pong helpers in this module, and otherwise drives FUN_004dd240 (service), FUN_004db180 (process incoming) and FUN_004dd330 (flush) once fully connected.
results.summary: Main per-tick network update for an actively-connected client: services the channel, processes incoming messages, flushes outgoing data, and (when a debug flag is set) periodically logs ping/latency/time-delta statistics.

results.name: network_game_server_update
results.evidence: Mirrors FUN_004daf80's call sequence (FUN_004dd110 service, FUN_004db180 process incoming, then FUN_004db310, then FUN_004d9400) without the debug-print block, and falls back to setting the DAT_00718fa4 error code when the channel looks dead -- the host-side counterpart of the client per-tick update.
results.summary: Per-tick network update used while acting as host/server: services the channel, drains incoming messages, updates per-machine state, and sends a periodic ping.

results.name: network_game_process_incoming_messages
results.evidence: Loops while the channel's ring buffer (param_1+0xadc, offsets 0xc/0x10) has data, reading each queued item's bit offset/size via FUN_004dcf10, extracting it bit-by-bit, and feeding each decoded byte into FUN_004db630 -- the same dispatcher that ultimately reaches the per-message-type decode handlers via FUN_004db6b0.
results.summary: Drains the channel's incoming ring buffer, extracting queued items bit-by-bit and dispatching each to the network-message/action processor.

results.name: network_game_client_update_machine_state
results.evidence: Checks and clears an expiring-connection flag at param_1+0xee4 (closing via FUN_004dd3f0 on timeout), then on a second timer/flag pair (0xeec/0xef4) either records a new machine id via datum_get (single-session case) or reuses a cached one, calls FUN_004dde70/FUN_004dde50, and otherwise re-issues the connect handshake via FUN_004dc8d0 with a cached wide-character name.
results.summary: Periodic bookkeeping for the local client's machine/session identity: expires a stale pending-close flag, then either refreshes or re-establishes the client's connection identity depending on whether a session object is active.

results.name: network_game_client_set_status_text
results.evidence: References the strings "Loading", "Connecting", "Connecting%s" and a run of dots ("................"), builds a progress string of up to 16 dots via strncpy and FUN_00496a80("Connecting%s", ...), and writes the DAT_00718f90/DAT_00718f8c globals used elsewhere as the join-flow UI status/state.
results.summary: Updates the on-screen join/connect status text ("Loading", "Connecting", or an animated "Connecting...") and the associated UI state machine based on an integer mode selector.

results.name: network_game_process_queue_entry
results.evidence: Routes on param_2: when 1, calls FUN_004db870 (which loops applying queued actions via FUN_004da320); when 0, checks FUN_004de420(0xfff) before calling FUN_004db6b0, the message-type decode switch -- i.e. this picks between treating an incoming queue entry as a game action to apply or a network message to decode.
results.prototype: unsigned int __cdecl network_game_process_queue_entry(int param_1, unsigned int param_2)
results.summary: Dispatches a single incoming queue entry either to the queued-game-action applier or to the network-message decode switch, depending on an entry-type flag.

results.name: network_game_message_decode_dispatch
results.evidence: Validates a 2-bit tag in the leading word of the buffer, then switches on a following type byte across roughly 18 cases (2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,0xa..0xd,0x16..0x19,0x21,0x22), calling each of the per-type decode handlers in this same file (FUN_004db9a0, FUN_004dba20, FUN_004dbc00, ... FUN_004dc4b0) by address.
results.summary: The central switch that dispatches a decoded incoming network-game message to the correct per-type handler based on a type byte in the packet.

results.name: network_game_apply_queued_actions
results.evidence: Loops up to a stored count (local_ac) pulling the next queued action via FUN_004ec510 and applying it via FUN_004da320 (the action dispatcher), tracking two flags per iteration and finally calling FUN_004d9340 (a generic abort/reset helper used across this module) when done or on failure.
results.prototype: char __cdecl network_game_apply_queued_actions(int param_1, int param_2, int *param_3)
results.summary: Drains and applies a bounded run of queued network-game actions, one per iteration, via the action dispatcher.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_beacon_reply
results.evidence: Only processes while the connection state (in_EAX+0xeda) is 0 (idle); decodes via the named data_packet_group_decode_packet using the network-game-messages group table, then forwards the payload straight into FUN_004da7d0, the function that adds/refreshes an entry in the 9-slot game-search results list -- consistent with handling an incoming LAN game-announcement broadcast while idle.
results.summary: Decodes an incoming game-announcement ("beacon") message received while idle and adds it to the discovered-games search list.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_pong_reply
results.evidence: Valid at connection states 0 or 3; decodes via data_packet_group_decode_packet then calls FUN_004d93b0, which updates fields at offsets 0xad2/0xad4/0xad8 that match the "samples received"/"current ping time" statistics printed by FUN_004daf80 -- i.e. this is the handler for an incoming ping-reply used to compute round-trip time.
results.summary: Decodes an incoming ping-reply (pong) message and updates the connection's round-trip-time/ping statistics.

results.name: network_game_update_and_broadcast_ping
results.evidence: Calls FUN_004ec590 to fetch a small record, conditionally updates a player-table entry's field 0x6e keyed by an id (local_58) into the table at DAT_0087a480, walks an iterator via the already-named data_iterator_next computing an elapsed-time delta into a +0xdc field, then builds a small record and calls FUN_004ec940(...) followed by FUN_004dcdb0 (the reliable-message buffer-pool store) to queue a short outgoing report.
results.summary: Updates a player-table ping/latency-related field, scans an iterator of entries to compute an elapsed-time delta, and queues a short reliable status message reporting it.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_server_info
results.evidence: Only valid while connection state (unaff_ESI+0xeda) equals 1; decodes via data_packet_group_decode_packet then calls FUN_004d94c0, which byte-compares a name against a cached table (DAT_00712dd8) and, on mismatch, advances the UI/menu state via FUN_004c87a0 -- consistent with receiving the server/map identification early in the join handshake.
results.summary: Decodes an early-handshake server/map identification message and compares it against locally cached data, advancing the loading UI state on a mismatch.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_join_accepted
results.evidence: Only valid while connection state equals 1; decodes via data_packet_group_decode_packet then calls FUN_004d9700, which validates a 0-15 index from the payload, stores it as the local player's assigned index, and sets that context's own state field to 2 -- the classic "server accepted your join, here is your slot" step of the handshake.
results.summary: Decodes the server's join-accepted message, assigning the local client its player slot index and advancing the connection to the next handshake state.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_connect_rejected
results.evidence: Valid except at states 0/4; decodes via data_packet_group_decode_packet then calls FUN_004d97e0, which sets the DAT_00718fa4 error code from the payload and unconditionally sets DAT_0071c2de and calls FUN_004aa900 (the same disconnect trigger used by other error paths in this file).
results.summary: Decodes a connect-rejected / error notification from the server and triggers the client disconnect path with the given error code.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_join_complete
results.evidence: Valid except at states 0/4; decodes via data_packet_group_decode_packet, then directly sets DAT_00718f8c (the join-flow UI state) to 9 and the connection-state field to 4, matching the code path other functions in this file treat as "fully connected / in game".
results.summary: Decodes the server's final join-complete confirmation and transitions the client to the in-game connection state.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_game_settings
results.evidence: When acting purely as a client at state 2 (DAT_00719720==2) it calls FUN_004d9f50 once per connection (guarded by a byte flag) instead of decoding; otherwise at states 2/3 it decodes via data_packet_group_decode_packet and forwards the payload to FUN_004d9800, which itself calls FUN_004c87a0 (menu/UI state advance) and FUN_004d9f50.
results.summary: Decodes an incoming game-settings/map-info message during the join handshake and applies it, sending a one-time acknowledgement when acting purely as a client.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_player_option
results.evidence: Only valid at connection state 2; decodes via data_packet_group_decode_packet and stores the low 16 bits of the decoded value directly into a field at offset 0xed8 of the connection context, with no further processing.
results.summary: Decodes a small per-player configuration value from the server and stores it directly into the connection context during the join handshake.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_message_0c
results.evidence: Only valid at connection state 2; calls data_packet_group_decode_packet and discards the result with no further handling -- effectively consumes the message without acting on its payload in this build.
results.summary: Decodes and discards a message type (0xc) received during the join handshake, taking no further action.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_message_0d
results.evidence: Only valid at connection state 4 (fully in-game); calls data_packet_group_decode_packet with group index 6 (versus 2 used by the join-handshake handlers) and takes no further action on the decoded payload.
results.summary: Decodes and discards an in-game message type (0xd) using a different message-group index than the join-handshake handlers.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_message_0a
results.evidence: Only valid at connection state 2; decodes via data_packet_group_decode_packet then forwards the payload to FUN_004d9960, a bool-returning function taking a ushort pointer whose result is passed straight back as this handler's return value.
results.summary: Decodes a join-handshake message (type 0xa) and forwards it to a secondary validation/processing routine, propagating its success/failure result.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_message_0b
results.evidence: Only valid at connection state 2; decodes via data_packet_group_decode_packet then calls FUN_004d9ce0 with no further handling of its return value.
results.summary: Decodes a join-handshake message (type 0xb) and forwards the payload to a follow-up handler.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_sync_chunk_a
results.evidence: Only valid at connection state 3 (synchronizing); decodes via data_packet_group_decode_packet with group index 4, forwards to FUN_004d9d20, and calls the shared abort helper FUN_004d9340 when that fails -- matching the pattern of two sibling handlers (0x4dc240, 0x4dc2e0) that decode with the same group index during the same state and share the same abort path.
results.summary: Decodes one of several similarly-structured synchronization-phase data chunks and aborts the connection attempt via a shared cleanup routine on failure.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_sync_chunk_b
results.evidence: Same structure as 0x4dc190 (decode group index 4 at state 3, share FUN_004d9340 abort on failure) but forwards the payload to a different follow-up handler, FUN_004d9e30; treats state 4 as an already-complete no-op.
results.summary: Decodes another synchronization-phase data chunk during the join handshake, aborting via the shared cleanup routine on failure.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_sync_chunk_c
results.evidence: Same structure as 0x4dc190/0x4dc240 (decode group index 4, share the FUN_004d9340 abort path) but accepted at states 2, 3 or 4 and forwards to FUN_004d9190.
results.summary: Decodes a third variant of synchronization-phase data chunk, accepted across a wider range of connection states.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_sync_complete
results.evidence: Only valid at connection state 3; decodes via data_packet_group_decode_packet with group index 4 and then unconditionally sets the connection-state field to 4, mirroring the state transition performed explicitly by the case-7 handler (0x4dbdc0).
results.summary: Decodes the final synchronization message of the join handshake and transitions the connection into the fully-connected/in-game state.

results.name: network_game_host_decode_client_command
results.evidence: Only valid at connection state 4 (in-game); decodes via data_packet_group_decode_packet with group index 6, and only when DAT_00719720==1 (acting as host) forwards the two decoded values to FUN_004d9ed0 -- clients receiving the same message type take no action.
results.summary: Decodes an in-game message and, only when acting as host, forwards its two payload values to a follow-up handler -- consistent with the host applying a command replicated by a client.

results.name: network_game_client_decode_game_over
results.evidence: Only valid at connection state 4; decodes via data_packet_group_decode_packet with group index 6, defaults a field at offset 0xedc to 8 if unset, and conditionally sets DAT_0071c2de and calls FUN_004aa900 (the same disconnect-trigger call used by the connect-rejected handler) unless a specific game-engine flag bit is already set.
results.summary: Decodes an in-game notification and, unless a particular game-engine state flag is already set, triggers the client disconnect/leave path -- consistent with a game-over or host-shutdown notice.

results.name: network_address_parse_port
results.evidence: Locates a delimiter via FUN_006257e0 (strchr-style) in a string reached through a hidden register argument, verifies every character after it is a digit via _isdigit, converts it with _atol, and validates the result is in the 1-65535 TCP/UDP port range before optionally storing it through the output pointer.
results.summary: Parses and range-checks a numeric port substring (after a delimiter) out of an address string, optionally writing the value through an output pointer.

results.name: network_address_string_normalize
results.evidence: Uses the format strings "%d.%d.%d.%d.%d", "%d.%d.%d.%d:%d" and "%d.%d.%d.%d" with sscanf/snprintf to parse four dotted-decimal octets (each range-checked 0-255), flags an all-zero (0.0.0.0) address through param_3, calls FUN_004dc560 to parse an optional trailing port, and writes a canonical "a.b.c.d" or "a.b.c.d:port" string to the output buffer.
results.summary: Parses a dotted-decimal IP address string (with an optional trailing port) and writes back a canonical "a.b.c.d" or "a.b.c.d:port" string, also reporting whether the address is the wildcard 0.0.0.0.

results.name: network_address_string_is_valid
results.evidence: First rejects an empty string, defers to FUN_004dc5e0 (dotted-IP normalization) for a quick accept, and otherwise walks the string accepting only '.', '-', ':' and alphanumeric characters via _isalnum -- a lenient validator for a typed IP-or-hostname[:port] address string.
results.summary: Validates that a user-supplied string looks like a legal IP address or hostname, optionally with a port suffix.

results.name: network_game_client_connect_to_address
results.evidence: Copies the input string to a local buffer, finds a ':' separator via FUN_006257e0 to split host from port, calls inet_addr and _atol (port) or FUN_00557990 (a hostname-resolution style call) depending on whether a colon was found, clears _DAT_006b2f28 when the address is null, and finally calls FUN_004dc8d0(param_1) to actually begin the connection.
results.summary: Parses a user-entered address[:port] string, resolves it to a numeric address, and kicks off the connect handshake.

results.name: network_game_connect_begin
results.evidence: Lazily creates/caches the client connection object via FUN_004d8a80 into DAT_0071c2d8, copies a large cached table (DAT_00712dd8) into a local scratch buffer, and when the connection is idle (eda==0) and the incoming request struct (in_ECX) looks valid, calls the already-named chimera__on_connect and, on success, sets DAT_00719720 to 1 (marking the network mode active); on failure it sets DAT_0071c2de and calls FUN_004aa900 to unwind.
results.summary: Begins a new outgoing connection attempt: allocates/reuses the client connection object, hands off to chimera__on_connect with the requested name/options, and marks the network session active on success.

results.name: network_channel_new
results.evidence: Allocates one of two struct sizes (0xae4 with flag bit 0, else 0xa9c) via GlobalAlloc keyed on param_1's low two bits, optionally sets up an event/overlap object via FUN_00441960, creates a socket via FUN_00441bf0 and (for the larger variant) binds/listens via FUN_00442170/FUN_00441a40, allocates an incoming circular_buffer_new("transport-incoming"), and initializes per-channel bookkeeping (fragment table, tick-count timestamp, two calls to FUN_004dd980) before returning the new channel or tearing it down via FUN_004dcae0 on any failure.
results.summary: Allocates and initializes a new network transport/channel object (socket, incoming buffer, bookkeeping) sized and configured according to the requested flag bits; frees everything and returns NULL on failure.

results.name: network_channel_delete
results.evidence: Recursively frees an array of up to 16 child channel pointers at offset 0x2a8 (calling itself and FUN_00441b00, a likely closesocket-style call, on each), frees the incoming circular buffer and an overlap/event object, frees a growable per-channel record array (offset 0x29e/0x29f), resets a large block of state fields, and finally frees the channel object itself via GlobalFree -- the destructor counterpart to FUN_004dc9b0.
results.summary: Tears down and frees a network channel object, recursively closing/freeing any child channels, its buffers, and associated OS handles before freeing the object itself.

results.name: network_channel_reliable_buffer_pool_acquire
results.evidence: Scans an array of 0x20-byte records at channel+0xa7c/0xa78 for a free (byte 0 == 0) entry whose two GlobalAlloc'd buffers (offsets 0x18/0x1c) are at least param_2/param_3 bytes, and if none is large enough grows the table by 10 new entries (each with two fresh GlobalAlloc buffers, minimum size 100) before returning; the same table (offsets 0xa78/0xa7c) is later scanned for retransmission by FUN_004dd9d0.
results.summary: Finds (or grows and allocates) a reusable pair of fixed-size scratch buffers in the channel's reliable-message buffer pool, sized to hold at least the requested header/body byte counts.

results.name: network_channel_reliable_buffer_pool_store
results.evidence: Converts two bit counts (in_EAX, in_ECX) to byte counts, calls FUN_004dcc30 to find/allocate a matching pool slot, marks it active (byte 0 = 1), tags it with param_4 (a small stream/category id matching the 10-bucket scan in FUN_004dd9d0), and copies the two payload buffers (param_2, param_3) into the slot's two scratch buffers.
results.summary: Stores a header/body message pair into a tagged slot of the channel's reliable-message buffer pool for later (re)transmission tracking.

results.name: network_channel_enqueue_message
results.evidence: Immediately returns success if the channel is flagged closed (offset 0xa8c bit 0); when param_4 == 1 it commits param_3 bytes directly to the outgoing queue via the shared FUN_004cf8f0/FUN_004ddb60 pattern (optionally flushing again if param_5 == 1), otherwise it defers to FUN_004dcdb0 to store the message in the reliable buffer pool instead.
results.summary: Queues an outgoing message either for immediate transmission or, when not marked immediate, into the reliable retransmission buffer pool, depending on a caller-supplied mode flag.

results.name: network_channel_receive_pending_bits
results.evidence: Checks the channel's ring buffer has pending bytes, then reads a 2-byte length prefix via the already-named circular_buffer_read, validates it against the buffer's contiguous available bytes, and reads the payload out via a second circular_buffer_read call -- exactly the per-item read FUN_004db180 uses in its drain loop before dispatching to FUN_004db630.
results.summary: Reads one length-prefixed item out of the channel's incoming ring buffer, used by the incoming-message processing loop before each item is dispatched.

results.name: network_channel_remove_child
results.evidence: Searches the 16-slot (0x11-bounded) child-channel table at unaff_EDI+0xaa0 for a pointer matching param_1, then calls FUN_00441b00 (closesocket-style) on its socket handle, clears an owning-channel flag byte, deletes it via FUN_004dcae0, and zeroes the table slot.
results.summary: Finds a specific child channel in the parent's child table, closes its socket, deletes the child object, and clears the table entry.

results.name: network_channel_service
results.evidence: Computes elapsed ms via QueryPerformanceCounter, updates and clears status-flag bits (offset 0xa8c) based on timeout thresholds, calls FUN_004dd9d0 (retransmit-timeout scan) and up to two FUN_004ddb60 flush calls guarded by byte flags, resets a running byte counter to 0xe0, and finally dispatches to FUN_004dd4e0 (receive) or FUN_004dd730 (transmit) depending on which status bits are set.
results.summary: Per-tick service routine for a network channel: updates timing/status flags, scans for and retransmits timed-out reliable messages, and dispatches to the receive or transmit path as needed.

results.name: network_channel_service_simple
results.evidence: Nearly identical to FUN_004dd110 (same elapsed-time/status-flag logic and the same dispatch to FUN_004dd4e0/FUN_004dd730) but omits the FUN_004dd9d0 retransmit scan and the FUN_004ddb60 flush calls, suggesting a lighter-weight variant used for a channel that doesn't need retransmit bookkeeping (e.g. a child/client channel versus the parent).
results.summary: A lighter-weight per-tick channel service routine, updating timing/status flags and dispatching to receive/transmit without the retransmit-timeout scan performed by the full channel service routine.

results.name: network_channel_flush
results.evidence: Reads a timestamp via QueryPerformanceCounter, calls FUN_004dd9d0 (retransmit scan) and up to two guarded FUN_004ddb60 flush calls exactly as in FUN_004dd110's tail, then resets the running byte counter to 0xe0, but performs no receive/transmit dispatch of its own.
results.summary: Runs the retransmit-timeout scan and pending-flush bookkeeping for a channel without performing an actual receive or transmit pass.

results.name: network_channel_message_precheck
results.evidence: Called 23 times, once at the top of nearly every per-type message decode handler in this file; when the channel's socket handle (in_EAX) is null, or a status check via FUN_00441ce0 (likely an ioctlsocket/FIONREAD-style query) returns non-zero, it fills the caller's local output record with a fixed "empty/type-4" sentinel value.
results.summary: Shared guard called before each per-message-type decode: fills the caller's local result record with a default sentinel value based on the channel's connectedness/pending-data state.

results.name: network_channel_reset_if_active
results.evidence: Checks the channel's flag word (in_EAX[0x2a3] bits 1/2) and that its socket handle is set and connected before calling FUN_004dd730 (transmit/flush) and then FUN_00442040 (an unnamed follow-up, likely socket shutdown or reconnect).
results.summary: If the channel is in an active connected/connecting state, flushes pending output and then performs a follow-up teardown/reconnect step.

results.name: network_channel_new_child
results.evidence: A simplified duplicate of the flag-bit-2 branch of FUN_004dc9b0: allocates the smaller (0xa9c) channel struct via GlobalAlloc, stores param_1 as its socket/owner id, sets its flag word to 4, creates its incoming buffer via circular_buffer_new("transport-incoming"), and performs the same bookkeeping initialization (tick-count timestamp, two FUN_004dd980 calls) before returning it or tearing it down via FUN_004dcae0 on failure; used by FUN_004dd4e0 to spin up a channel object for a freshly-accepted incoming connection.
results.summary: Allocates and initializes a new child network channel object for a freshly-accepted incoming connection, mirroring the smaller-variant setup done by the general channel constructor.

results.name: network_channel_receive
results.evidence: Calls FUN_004419d0 (an accept/recv-style Winsock call returning -0xd on WSAEWOULDBLOCK) and then loops over a queue of up to 16 pending completion records (channel+0x2a7 based), routing self-addressed events either to a per-channel callback function pointer (piVar2[2]) or FUN_00442250, spinning up a new child channel via FUN_004421b0+FUN_004dd430 for a fresh incoming connection, and otherwise forwarding data to the matching child channel via FUN_004dd730, closing the child on failure.
results.summary: Processes pending incoming-connection and data events on a channel, accepting new child connections and forwarding received data to the matching existing child channel.

results.name: network_channel_transmit
results.evidence: Repeatedly pulls up to 0x5000 bytes at a time out of a source buffer (offsets 0xc/0x8/0x10 ring-buffer fields) into a large local staging buffer and calls the already-named circular_buffer_write to push it onward, tracking a per-channel timestamp via QueryPerformanceCounter/__alldiv on each iteration until the source is empty or a channel/queue flag stops the loop.
results.summary: Pumps queued outgoing bytes for a channel from its internal ring buffer into the underlying transport's write queue in bounded-size chunks.

results.name: network_channel_record_timestamp
results.evidence: Computes the current time in milliseconds via QueryPerformanceCounter/__allmul/__alldiv and stores it into the channel struct at offset 4 -- the same field several other functions in this file compare against to detect timeouts.
results.summary: Records the current time (in milliseconds) into a channel's timestamp field, used elsewhere for timeout comparisons.

results.name: network_channel_init_stats
results.evidence: Defaults the global DAT_0071c2cc to 0xb if unset, then resets a small per-item record (pointer to self+0x1d, window-size fields defaulted to 0x287f/0x2880, a flag byte set to 1) and calls FUN_004cf8f0(DAT_0071c2cc) -- called twice from each channel constructor to initialize a pair of send/receive-style bookkeeping records.
results.summary: Initializes a small per-direction bookkeeping record (window sizes, flags) for a newly-created channel and primes the shared output queue with a default byte count.

results.name: network_channel_scan_retransmit_timeouts
results.evidence: Iterates the channel's reliable buffer-pool table (offsets 0xa78/0xa7c, the same table populated by FUN_004dcc30/FUN_004dcdb0) across 10 stream/category buckets, computes an expected-delivery time from a bytes-per-second rate (DAT_00710308 or a per-index rate table) and GetTickCount, and re-enqueues (via FUN_004cf8f0 twice, header then body) any entry whose data is overdue, before clearing every active-flag byte in the table.
results.summary: Scans the channel's reliable-message buffer pool for entries that are overdue based on an estimated delivery rate and retransmits them, then clears the pool's active flags.
